body.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(1\le g\le J+1\), \(p_X(x)>\kappa_0\), \(p_g(x)\in(\epsilon_0,1-\epsilon_0)\), \(\max_{g,t}E_{P_{0,O}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]<M_4\), \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0\), every nonzero eigenvalue of \(\Omega_x\) is greater than \(\kappa_0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) is locally constant, the common class \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty, and every estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) has asymptotic variance at least \(V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_U^2]\). At the intersection, \(C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x)=C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x)\) and hence \(\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0\). If \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\) solves \(\mathrm{QP}_x\), then \[\phi_U=\chi_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\chi_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\},\] and \[V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\chi_0^2]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.\] Relative to the alternative-hypothesis laws for the one integrated estimator in SunXieZhang2025, this is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark at the stated strict-interior constant-rank intersection law for procedures regular under PT-or-SC uncertainty. It neither replaces the branch-specific asymptotic variances, furnishes an implemented standard error, nor proves attainment or multiplier validity.
body.justification: The theorem gives the local price of PT-or-SC regularity at strict-interior constant-rank intersections: common composition variance plus finite centered projection values.
body.gap: The integrated-estimator laws in SunXieZhang2025 do not supply this sharp union-regular lower bound.
body.consumer: RummoEtAl2026 can benchmark a candidate union-regular procedure on the repaired subclass; the result does not replace the branch-specific variances of the integrated Sun--Xie--Zhang estimator or deliver inference.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(E_0=E_{P_{0,O}}\), \(u=J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\), and \(\mu_{C,t}(x)=(\mu_{2,t}(x),\ldots,\mu_{J+1,t}(x))^{\prime}\).  The strict-interior hypotheses ensure all conditioning probabilities and inverses used below are well defined, and they are precisely the hypotheses under which \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\) applies.

We first identify the causal target.  Under conditional parallel trends and no anticipation,
\[
 \delta_1^0(x)=\Delta\mu_g(x),
 \qquad g=2,\ldots,J+1,
 \tag{1}
\]
and therefore
\[
 E_F[Y_T(1)-Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]
 =\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{1,T-1}(x)-u^{\prime}D(x)
 =C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x).
 \tag{2}
\]
Because \(\pi_1=\sum_xp_X(x)p_1(x)>0\), averaging (2) over \(X\mid G=1\) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)\) on the PT branch.

Under the synthetic-mean restriction, the intercept and preperiod equations give \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\).  The strict SC Gram margin makes \(B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\) invertible, so the displayed formula uniquely identifies \(w(x)\).  The final-period equation gives
\[
 E_F[Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]=w(x)^{\prime}\mu_{C,T}(x),
 \tag{3}
\]
so the conditional causal effect is \(C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x)\).  Averaging proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O)\) on the SC branch.  At \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), both expressions equal the same conditional causal effect in every occupied stratum, whence
\[
 C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x)=C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x),
 \qquad
 \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0.
 \tag{4}
\]

Define the centered stratum faces
\[
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a,
 \qquad
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d.
 \tag{5}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\), adding \(\chi_0\) to sums of these faces exhausts the two influence classes.  We prove that they meet.  Suppress \(x\) and the positive stratum factor.  Adding a PT normal permits every donor weight \(v\) satisfying \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}v=1\), and the corresponding conditional-mean differential is
\[
 L_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)=\dot\mu_{1,T}-\dot\mu_{1,T-1}
 -v^{\prime}(\dot\mu_{C,T}-\dot\mu_{C,T-1}).
 \tag{6}
\]
For SC, differentiation of \(a=Bw\) gives
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w).
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently its affine face consists of differentials
\[
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q)=\dot\mu_{1,T}-w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T}
 +q^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w),
 \qquad B^{\prime}q=-\mu_{C,T}.
 \tag{8}
\]
At the intersection, (1) gives \(\mu_{C,T}=\mu_{C,T-1}+\delta_x\mathbf 1_J\).  If \(e_0\) selects the intercept row and \(e_-\) the period-\(T-1\) row, then
\[
 q_*=-e_- -\delta_xe_0,
 \qquad B^{\prime}q_*=-\mu_{C,T}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The intercept rows are fixed, so \(e_0^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w)=0\).  Substitution into (8) yields
\[
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q_*)
 =\dot\mu_{1,T}-\dot\mu_{1,T-1}
 -w^{\prime}(\dot\mu_{C,T}-\dot\mu_{C,T-1})
 =L_{\mathrm{PT}}(w).
 \tag{10}
\]
Restoring the stratum factor, equality of these continuous linear functionals for all scores implies equality of their Riesz representatives in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\).  The product-rule contribution is the common term \(\chi_0\) in (4), so the full influence classes have a nonempty intersection.

By the definitions of \(h_x\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(c(a,d)\),
\[
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)
 =c(a,d)^{\prime}h_x,
 \tag{11}
\]
and positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
 \Omega_x^{1/2}c(a,d)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E_0[\{\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\}^2\mid X=x]=0.
 \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) minimizes exactly the conditional squared norm of a common centered representative.  Feasibility follows from (10).  Orthogonal projection onto the finite-dimensional closed affine feasible image gives a unique minimum represented function; the Euclidean minimum-norm convention selects coefficients when displayed rows are redundant.  The locally constant rank and strict nonzero-eigenvalue margin keep this coordinate representation stable at the theorem point.

Different strata have disjoint support.  Conditional-residual normalization also gives
\[
 E_0[\chi_0\psi^{\circ}_{b,x}(a)]
 =E_0\!\left[\chi_0E_0\{\psi^{\circ}_{b,x}(a)\mid G,X\}\right]=0.
 \tag{13}
\]
The global projection therefore separates into the common composition component and the stratum programs:
\[
 \phi_U=\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^U)
 =\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^U),
 \tag{14}
\]
and
\[
 V_U(P_0)=E_0[\chi_0^2]+\sum_xp_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.
 \tag{15}
\]

Finally, an estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) is regular along every quadratic-mean differentiable submodel in either branch, so its influence component belongs to both derivative classes.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}semiparametric\text{-}convolution\text{-}bound}\) to finite collections of such paths and then taking their closed span gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}(\text{regular limit})
 \ge \inf_{\phi\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)}E_0[\phi^2]
 =E_0[\phi_U^2].
 \tag{16}
\]
This proves the sharp lower bound in the stated strict-interior local tangent experiment.  The cited Sun--Xie--Zhang result concerns one integrated ATT estimator and one multiplier construction analyzed under alternative PT and SC hypotheses, with potentially different branch influence functions and variances.  The present projection supplies neither an implemented standard error nor an attainment or multiplier-validity theorem.
